_about: Known fixes at the game <-> system-library boundary, keyed by the imported NID. Per library function, never per game. Read by Ps5Backport.Core. Fields: kind (stub | swap | adapter | redirect | plt_stub = stub body in a cave and the PLT entry jumps to it, the GOT slot is left alone: forces a value even where the target firmware has the function | none = only in an option: removes the default fix for that NID), name, area, sources (keys of "sources" or free text), stub (a name in stubs.json, or "ret:<value>"), new_nid (swap/adapter target), new_library (optional target import library; reuse its existing library/module suffix), export_nid (redirect target, exported by the same module), insns (adapter code, one "hex  ; asm" per instruction, branch-free; "call_got" = call the real function through its GOT slot), when (missing = only when the import is missing on the target [default] | always = argument fixes), below (optional firmware: apply only when the target is lower, e.g. 5.00), post_call (adapter runs after the real function), proven (default true; false = derived, not console-tested), note, rationale. "options": opt-in groups (never applied by default; selected per backport). Each has name, description, warning, sources and its own fixes (a selected option's fixes replace the default fix for the same NID), optionally fakelib_variant (files in the fakelib set's <variant>/ subfolder replace the same-named fakelibs) and patterns (byte replacements: find/replace hex; in modules only 4-aligned hits inside non-executable segments, in the listed data files every hit). "patterns": byte replacements applied with the known fixes (name, area, sources, find/replace hex, code = search executable segments at any offset instead of 4-aligned data, note, rationale); the find bytes carry enough context to match one function only.

tU5e3f9gSiU.name: sceKernelIsTrinityMode
tU5e3f9gSiU.note: PS5 Pro query (libkernel from FW 7.01); 0 = not Pro

3WVD91e12ZQ.name: scePsmlMfsrInit
3WVD91e12ZQ.rationale: libScePsml first appears in FW 9.00. Most games call scePsmlMfsrInit only on a PS5 Pro (behind sceKernelIsTrinityMode or a Pro flag), so with Trinity stubbed to 0 they never reach it. Kingdom Come: Deliverance II calls sceSysmoduleLoadModule(0x137) and then scePsmlMfsrInit on every console, and its tester replaced the call with return 0. plt_stub because the Psml fakelib provides the function. Lifted by the force_pro option (REFERENCE_OVERVIEW Part 28).

La9uyZv4Kvw.name: sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask
La9uyZv4Kvw.note: CPU affinity mask of the process (FW 12.40+): the firmware returns 0xff for a native title (0x1fff otherwise)
La9uyZv4Kvw.rationale: FW 12.70 libkernel computes the mask once from the app info: 0xff or 0x1fff, never 0 for a game. Callers pass it to thread-affinity calls; one game checks popcnt(mask) >= 5, so ret0 breaks it. A FW 4.03 backport (console-tested) returns 0xff; an earlier backport's ret0 only worked because its caller just forwards the value.

XgVs4jRehcY.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait16
XgVs4jRehcY.rationale: Names from AnyPS5 (NIDs computed; not in aerolib). FreeBSD _umtx_op has no 8/16-bit compare, so Wait8/Wait16 stay return-0 stubs as in CONTROL (callers re-check and spin).

dFym5b41JLU.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait8
dFym5b41JLU.rationale: Names from AnyPS5 (NIDs computed; not in aerolib). FreeBSD _umtx_op has no 8/16-bit compare, so Wait8/Wait16 stay return-0 stubs as in CONTROL (callers re-check and spin).

-q-vbO859Tw.name: libSceVideoOutVrrStatus -q-vbO859Tw
-q-vbO859Tw.note: VRR status query (FW 5.02 and later have it): return 0, like the other two VrrStatus functions

w7Ipp9Xl7hg.name: sceVideoOutAllowOutputResolutionWqhdDetection
w7Ipp9Xl7hg.note: no WQHD output detection: return 0 (FW 6.00 and later have it)

IXmfUaze9So.name: sceNpCommerceDialogOpen2
IXmfUaze9So.note: store dialog unavailable: returns an error (FW 7.01 and later have it)

fCWdlnmB1Ks.name: scePadIsRemoteController
fCWdlnmB1Ks.note: not a remote controller: *isRemote = 0, return 0 (FW 10.01 and later have it)
fCWdlnmB1Ks.rationale: BF6 4xx+ routes the PLT entry through a guard that calls the real function when its GOT slot is bound and otherwise does mov byte [rsi], 0; xor eax, eax; ret. The stub is that fallback.

D1IAo-CNswA.name: sceHttp2WebSocketSendDataMessage
D1IAo-CNswA.note: online disabled: returns an error (FW 5.02 and later have it)

jSHMX1oSE+E.name: sceHttp2WebSocketSendTextMessage
jSHMX1oSE+E.note: online disabled: returns an error (FW 5.02 and later have it)

v2hFBiyS13w.name: sceHttp2WebSocketClose
v2hFBiyS13w.note: online disabled: returns an error (FW 5.02 and later have it)

bEegosRhgM0.name: sceHttp2SetRequestNoContentLength
bEegosRhgM0.note: FW 5.02 and later have it; marks an HTTP/2 request as having no Content-Length
bEegosRhgM0.rationale: A Unity PS5 player calls it once, only for a request without a known length (the other branch calls sceHttp2SetRequestContentLength), and ignores the result in both branches; that game's FW 4.xx backport left it unpatched (lazy binding: it fails only if called). Returning 0 skips the flag.

4h6F1LLbTiw.name: sceKernelMapNamedFlexibleMemoryInternal
4h6F1LLbTiw.rationale: libc's heap growth passes flags 0x8000, which only the internal entry accepts: the public sceKernelMapFlexibleMemory masks flags with 0xffbfff6f on FW 1.00-6.50 and rejects 0x88000 outright on FW 12.70, returning 0x80020016 (EINVAL) on every firmware, so a plain swap fails as soon as libc grows its heap ('Failed to create the heap', 0xa002000e). The swap is console-proven where that path was not taken; a FW 4.03 backport (console-tested) cleared the flag at both call sites, and so does this adapter.

B2n8aDorSH4.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait32
B2n8aDorSH4.rationale: GT7's exact register transforms to _umtx_op op 11 (WAIT_UINT); CONTROL stubbed it to return 0.

PZQhiiLXRFs.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait64
PZQhiiLXRFs.rationale: GT7's exact register transforms to _umtx_op op 2 (WAIT); CONTROL stubbed it to return 0.

q2y-wDIVWZA.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWake
q2y-wDIVWZA.rationale: GT7's exact register transforms to _umtx_op op 3 (WAKE); CONTROL stubbed it to return 0.

Hc4CaR6JBL0.name: sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait
Hc4CaR6JBL0.rationale: AnyPS5 shows the generic Wait has Wait32's signature (u32* addr, u32 expected, KernelUseconds* timeout, name), so it gets Wait32's translation (the console-proven Wait32 path, op 11 WAIT_UINT). GT7's own patch passed `expected` as the _umtx_op op code (spins instead of sleeping).

-sD02mFDBh4.name: sceUserServiceGetGamePresets
-sD02mFDBh4.rationale: Argument fix: newer SDKs pass a 0x30-byte struct (size field first); a FW 4.xx backport changed the game's size from 0x30 to 0x28 at its only call site. The size check is in the system service (the FW 4.03 library forwards the call over IPC), so the first firmware that accepts 0x30 is unknown; the original game runs on 11.xx, hence below 11.00. The game zeroes the struct first and reads back only the first 0x28 bytes. rax = [rsi]; if rax > 0x28: rax = 0x28; [rsi] = rax.

uv0Ae+jCeWY.name: sceHmd2ReprojectionSetAllowPositionalReprojection
uv0Ae+jCeWY.note: FW 6.50 and later have it; PSVR2 reprojection setting
uv0Ae+jCeWY.rationale: A PSVR2 game's FW 4.xx/5.xx backport wraps the import in a guard that returns 0 when the loader left it unresolved and calls the real function otherwise. A console-tested FW 4 backport of a game with an optional VR mode left it unpatched (never called without a headset); a VR-only game calls it, so returning 0 (success, setting ignored) is the fallback.

gWT7X8H0bYs.name: sceVideoOutGetOutputStatusWithVrr
gWT7X8H0bYs.note: VRR status getter (FW 10.01): zero the 0x50-byte status, i.e. VRR off
gWT7X8H0bYs.rationale: FW 10.01 libSceVideoOut: (handle, status*); the export returns an error without writing when VideoOut is not initialised or status is null, otherwise the implementation writes exactly 0x50 bytes (+0x00..+0x30 and a 32-byte block at +0x30). A game calling it ignores the return value and reads the struct (+0x04 == 2, bit 0x10 at +0x10, words at +0x30..+0x34), sometimes from uninitialised stack, so ret0 alone is not enough; an all-zero status takes the game's 'VRR off' path. Derived from the firmware code, not console-tested.

ubisoft_offline_popups.name: Ubisoft offline popups
ubisoft_offline_popups.description: Suppresses MUFFIN-4520 and MUFFIN-4521 using the existing silent-error callbacks in recognized Unity/Esut Ubisoft code. Detects linked code patterns without a game ID or fixed address.
ubisoft_offline_popups.warning: Opt-in. Requires Known fixes. Suppresses these two warnings only; online services remain unavailable when authentication fails. Tested on Rogue Prince of Persia; other matching games require console verification. Does not fix progress saving.
sources: Rogue Prince of Persia 01.006.000 PPSA28155: Ghidra analysis and console-confirmed popup suppression

unity_sku_offline.name: Unity unset-SKU offline fallback
unity_sku_offline.description: Allows recognized Unity/Esut authentication code to use its existing recoverable startup path when the platform reports an unset SKU. Detects linked code patterns rather than a game ID or fixed address; leaves trial and full-game results unchanged.
unity_sku_offline.warning: Opt-in. Console-tested on The Rogue Prince of Persia 01.006.000 (PPSA28155); other games require testing. Unrecognized or ambiguous code is left unchanged. Online-service warnings may still appear.
sources: The Rogue Prince of Persia 01.006.000 PPSA28155, user console-tested guarded NotSet fallback

save_mount_compat.name: Save mount compatibility
save_mount_compat.description: Changes sceSaveDataMount3 systemBlocks from -1 to 0 on target firmware below 5.00. Requires Known fixes enabled.
save_mount_compat.warning: Disabled by default. Derived adapter, not console-tested. Without it, old firmware may reject a save-mount request using -1. Disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.
sources: Existing save-data argument adapter; console testing pending

ZP4e7rlzOUk.name: sceSaveDataMount3
ZP4e7rlzOUk.rationale: Argument fix: the function exists on old firmware but rejects values newer SDKs pass (AC README: ShellCore rejects -1 when the game SDK is below 5.00, hence below 5.00). All three games patched this at the call site in their own code; doing it at the import boundary covers every game. rax = [rdi+0x18]; r11 = rax+1; if r11 == 0 (value was -1): rax = 0; [rdi+0x18] = rax.

save_prepare_compat.name: Save preparation compatibility
save_prepare_compat.description: Changes sceSaveDataPrepare preparation mode 2 to 1 before the native call. Requires Known fixes enabled.
save_prepare_compat.warning: Disabled by default. Derived adapter, not console-tested. Without it, the native save-preparation call may reject mode 2. Disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.
sources: Existing save-data argument adapter; console testing pending

sDCBrmc61XU.name: sceSaveDataPrepare
sDCBrmc61XU.rationale: Argument fix (CONTROL patched the call site). eax = [rsi+4]; if eax == 2: eax = 1; [rsi+4] = eax (r11 scratch).

audio_speaker_compat.name: Audio speaker compatibility
audio_speaker_compat.description: Limits the reported speaker configuration to eight speakers and clears the 3D-audio flag after sceAudioOut2GetSpeakerInfo. Optional so dialogue issues can be compared with this adapter enabled or disabled. Requires Known fixes enabled.
audio_speaker_compat.warning: Experimental; this adapter is derived and not console-tested. Disabled by default. Without it, some old-SDK games may select an unsupported audio layout and lose sound. Required missing audio API stubs and other existing audio fixes remain active. Re-cook from the same source for each test; disabling does not undo patches already present in the input.

DImz2Ft9E2g.name: sceAudioOut2GetSpeakerInfo
insns: 57  ; push rdi (SpeakerInfo*; also aligns the stack)
call_got  ; call the real function through its GOT slot
DImz2Ft9E2g.rationale: On newer firmware the OS reports 3D audio / 7.1.4 speakers, the game then opens a 12-channel AudioOut2 port, and an old-SDK binary is refused: no sound (CONTROL README; CONTROL fixed it inside Wwise). The game decides from GetSpeakerInfo (CONTROL eboot 0x3ca27f1: flags & 1 = 3D audio, popcnt(available_bits) > 8 = height speakers; struct layout from AnyPS5). Post-call fix: run the real function, then clear the 3D flag and cap the report at 8 speakers. Derived from references, not console-tested.

auto_pro.name: Automatic Pro mode
auto_pro.description: Keeps native console-mode queries when available, so the game can choose its base PS5 or PS5 Pro path at runtime. Missing queries fall back to base-console values. Keeps the default Psml initialization guard below firmware 9.00. Requires Known fixes enabled.
auto_pro.warning: Experimental; test on both console types. Queries missing from the selected target fall back to fixed base-console answers, even if this cook later runs on a Pro with newer firmware. Preserves automatic selection only for queries the target supports. Replacement libraries must report the actual console correctly. Cannot be combined with Force PS5 Pro mode.
sources: Native hardware queries with base-console fallback; console testing pending

force_pro.name: Force PS5 Pro mode
force_pro.description: Makes the game treat the console as a PS5 Pro (Pro graphics mode, PSSR when the game supports it): sceKernelGetOperationMode reports mode 3, sceKernelIsTrinityMode and sceAgcGetIsTrinityMode report true, and scePsmlMfsrInit is called again (the default skips it below FW 9.00).
force_pro.warning: PS5 Pro only. On a base PS5 or Slim, or on a Pro firmware where the game's PSSR path fails, the game shows a black screen. PSSR may also need a newer libScePsml fakelib and the PSSR model file.

3WVD91e12ZQ.name: scePsmlMfsrInit
3WVD91e12ZQ.note: keeps the real init (PSSR needs it)

gpu_scratch.name: GPU compute scratch fix (firmware below 12)
gpu_scratch.description: Uses the fakelib set's libSceAgcDriver variant that hooks command-buffer submission and gives compute shaders a 24 MB scratch area (older firmware sets none up), and turns every s_trap 1 (asserts in the SDK's ray-tracing BVH shaders) into s_nop in the game's modules and ShaderData.bin.
gpu_scratch.warning: Not needed by most games. Use it when a game hangs or shows a black screen during GPU work on firmware below 12. Needs a fakelib set with a gpu_scratch variant (fakelibs/4, fakelibs/4.03).

playgo_0_6.name: PlayGo 0.6 (experimental)
playgo_0_6.description: Replaces libScePlayGo.sprx with the official 0.6 build, adding synchronized lifecycle handling and empty-list compatibility. Keeps the current library unless selected.
playgo_0_6.warning: Console compatibility is unverified. Available in the 4, 4.03, 7, 9.60, 10 and 11 store sets. Select either this option or PlayGo 0.6 logging. Uses an existing /app0/playgo_stub.dat when present; no config is generated.

playgo_0_6_log.name: PlayGo 0.6 logging (experimental)
playgo_0_6_log.description: Uses the official 0.6 logging build under the runtime name libScePlayGo.sprx. Writes /app0/playlgo.log (upstream spelling) for one diagnostic run.
playgo_0_6_log.warning: Console compatibility is unverified. Logging changes timing and writes /app0/playlgo.log (upstream spelling). Available in the 4, 4.03, 7, 9.60, 10 and 11 store sets. Select either this option or normal PlayGo 0.6; collect the log and disable this option after testing. No config is generated.

patterns.name: Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 (speaker setup)
patterns.note: Wwise speaker setup: 7.1.4 (12 channels) -> 7.1, which an SDK-4 binary can open
patterns.rationale: A newer OS reports 3D audio, so Wwise picks 7.1.4 (channel mask 0x2d63f10c); a port opened by a low-SDK binary is refused at 12 channels and there is no sound. The mask becomes 7.1 (0x63f108). Same Wwise build in CONTROL (patched the speaker-setup site), Beast of Reincarnation and Borderlands 4 (both sites; BL4 also the packed default below).

patterns.name: Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 (channel switch)
patterns.note: Wwise speaker setup: 7.1.4 (12 channels) -> 7.1, which an SDK-4 binary can open
patterns.rationale: A newer OS reports 3D audio, so Wwise picks 7.1.4 (channel mask 0x2d63f10c); a port opened by a low-SDK binary is refused at 12 channels and there is no sound. The mask becomes 7.1 (0x63f108). Same Wwise build in CONTROL (patched the speaker-setup site), Beast of Reincarnation and Borderlands 4 (both sites; BL4 also the packed default below).

patterns.name: Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 (packed default)
patterns.note: Wwise speaker setup: 7.1.4 (12 channels) -> 7.1, which an SDK-4 binary can open
patterns.rationale: movabs rdx, 0x2d63f10c2d63f10c (two 7.1.4 masks) stored as a default; Borderlands 4 changes the low one to 7.1 (0x63f108). CONTROL and Beast left it, so it is the least proven of the three Wwise sites.

patterns.name: EA Sports Frostbite: 0x30c output buffer 0xc00 -> 0x800
patterns.note: probably 12 -> 8 audio channels (format 0x30c), the Frostbite counterpart of the Wwise 7.1.4 -> 7.1 fix
patterns.rationale: In the branch taken when a global format equals 0x30c (read as type 3, 12 channels; 0x201 nearby), a size field [rbp-0xf0] is set to 0xc00 (12 x 0x100); both EA Sports backports set 0x800 (8 x 0x100). The meaning is inferred from the values, not traced. UFC 6 tested on a PS5 Pro at FW 9.60; FC 27 ships it in both its backports. Not in Battlefield 6 (different code).
